key_insight: Validated RFSSW settings for AA6061-T6/AZ31B-H24 show that joint performance is governed by a tradeoff between higher heat input and preserving a solid-state bond window.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical process window for lightweight Al–Mg dissimilar joining in transport and aerospace, where avoiding brittle intermetallic growth is critical.
method: Built a 2D axisymmetric, fully coupled thermomechanical FEM model in Simufact Forming 2025.2
Varied tool rotational speed, sleeve penetration depth, and welding time across the RFSSW process window
Validated simulated thermal peaks against embedded thermocouples and infrared thermography
evidence_signal: Measured and predicted peak temperatures agreed within about 5%, and lap-shear testing showed a maximum load of 3.08 kN with best strength-toughness balance at 2.6 mm penetration and 4 s welding time.
watch_item: At the hottest settings, local interfacial temperatures can enter the Al–Mg eutectic range, so parameter increases risk transient liquation and brittle intermetallic formation.
paper_title: Process Parameter Optimization in Refill Friction Stir Spot Welding of 6061-T6 Aluminum Alloy and AZ31B-H24 Magnesium Alloy Dissimilar Joints
